grammar.title: Comparatives and Superlatives
grammar.explanation:
We use **comparatives** to compare two things. The scarf is warmer than the coat.

For short words, add **-er** to the word. Warm becomes **warmer**. Big becomes **bigger**.

For long words, use **more** or **less**. This keyboard is **more expensive** than my old one.

We use **superlatives** to say something is number one. She is **the fastest** typist in the office.

For short words use **the** + **-est**. The belt is **the cheapest** in the shop. For long words use **the most**. The laptop is **the most expensive**.

A common mistake: say **bigger than**, not *more bigger*. Say **the best**, not *the most best*.
examples: The scarf is *warmer* than the coat. (warm → warmer)
This belt is *cheaper* than that belt. (cheap → cheaper)
An email is *quicker* than a letter. (quick → quicker)
My keyboard is *more expensive* than my mouse. (long words use more)
She is the *tallest* girl in the class. (tall → the tallest)
The laptop is the *most expensive* in the shop. (long words: the most)

practice.q: Complete: The scarf is ___ than the coat. (warm / warmer)
practice.a: Warmer. Say: The scarf is warmer than the coat.

practice.q: Complete: This keyboard is ___ expensive than my old one. (more / most)
practice.a: More. Say: This keyboard is more expensive than my old one.

practice.q: Complete: He is the ___ boy in the class. (taller / tallest)
practice.a: Tallest. Say: He is the tallest boy in the class.

practice.q: Complete: An email is ___ than a letter. (quick / quicker)
practice.a: Quicker. Say: An email is quicker than a letter.
